title: Time-slice two programs on one toy CPU
brief: Save and restore CPU registers, then build a Machine that shares one CPU between programs using a timer interrupt.
hints: A context is the CPU's entire private state: the four registers and the program counter. `save_context` copies them out; `restore_context` copies them back in.
Copy the register list with `list(cpu.regs)` or `cpu.regs[:]`. If you store `cpu.regs` itself, the later run of another program changes your saved copy.
`restore_context` must also set `cpu.halted = False`. A process that is being restored has not halted.

`next_runnable` scans from `current + 1` forward, wrapping with `% len(procs)`, and checks `procs[i].done`. Scan `len(procs)` positions so the current process is the last candidate. With `current = -1` the scan starts at process 0.

In `Machine.run`: restore the context, then run up to `quantum` instructions or until the CPU halts. That is the timer interrupt: the CPU is taken away after `quantum` instructions even if the program has more to do.
After a slice, save the context. Mark the process done if `cpu.halted` is set. Otherwise count one timer interrupt. Append `(pid, instructions_run)` to `self.schedule`.
